Applicant :- Girraj

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Rajiv Kumar Pandey
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Vivek Varma,J. 
1.
Supplementary affidavit filed by the learned counsel for the applicant is taken on record.

2. Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. for the State-opposite party and perused the record.
3.

The instant bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. has been filed with the prayer to enlarge the applicant on bail in S.T. No. 282 of 2006, arising out of Case Crime No. 134 of 2003, under Sections 420, 272, 273 I.P.C. and 7/12 Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, Police Station Atrauli,
District Aligarh during the pendency of the trial.

Girraj vs State Of U.P. on 6 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57774662/
1 4.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that earlier the applicant was granted bail by the trial Court on 24.09.2003.
Though the applicant participated in the trial till 2021, the trial could not conclude and at the same time due to unavoidable reasons the applicant had left the station to earn livelihood.
As such the applicant was reported to have absconded and has surrendered again on 01.08.2023 and since then he is in jail.

Learned counsel for the applicant on the basis of instructions submits that if the applicant is enlarged on bail, he shall appear regularly before the court below and shall not leave the station without permission of the court concerned.
5. Learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail but could not satisfactorily dispute the aforesaid submissions from the record.

6. Having heard counsel for the parties and having perused the record, this Court prima facie finds that the applicant had earlier appeared and contested the proceedings, however, the trial could not conclude and further the applicant has presently remained confined for more than two months and there is no hope of early conclusion of trial, more so when no reasonable apprehension has been brought to the fore by the State that the applicant, if enlarged on bail, would either tamper with the evidence or intimidate the witness, without commenting on the merits of the case, I am of the opinion that the applicant is entitled to be enlarged on bail.

Order Date :- 6.10.2023 SKT/-
